text.p: - These are leading stories in this morning's Paris
-- Retail chain But chairman Michel Venturini in an interview denies rumours about plans to sell company to British partner Kingfisher.
-- Defence Minister Alain Richard said he favours an alliance between Dassault and Aerospatiale but sees it happening while keeping Aerospatiale in the public sector.
-- Guinness and GrandMet seen ready for talks with LVMH about merger plans in wines and spirits.
-- British retailer Kingfisher seen keen to buy But for an estimated two billion francs.

-- U.S. cocoa processing group Cargill enters capital of Ivory Coast exporter SICC, gaining control of cocoa supply for its European plants and jeopardizing growth of competing Franco-Swiss group Barry-Callebaut in Europe.
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin names advisory council of 52 economists to advise on economic policy options.
-- Insurance broker Gras Savoye to sell a 32 percent stake to Britain's Willis Corroon to develop international services.
-- Oil group Elf Aquitaine sells remaining 1.2 percent stake in Renault.
-- Liffe chairman Jack Wigglesworth in an interview says pit trading is the fastest and most efficient way of registering high volumes of transactions.
-- Caisse des Depots et Consignations to contribute some two billion francs to curbing public deficit, Finance Ministry said yesterday.
-- LVMH is seen as having spent 12 billion francs so far in increasing its stakes in Guinness and GrandMet in bid to hamper their merger.
